# Template: note_sheet
A treble-clef staff with notes computed from a simple notation string — "C4:q D4:q E4:h" (pitch letter + optional #/b + octave, duration w/h/q/e/s = 4/2/1/half/quarter beats, chords joined with +, R for rests) — with correct staff positions, ledger lines, stems, open vs filled heads, bar lines by time signature, and optional letter names under the notes — or a whole tune given as ABC notation via the `abc` param (first voice rendered; key signatures become explicit accidentals). Pair it with a `play` command carrying the SAME notation (or the same {abc}) so viewers hear what they see. Choose this scene for ANY request about sheet music, staff or musical notation, notes/scales/melodies/chords written on a staff, reading music, note durations, or a named tune in ABC. With keyboard: true a compact piano sits below the staff, and each note also gets a key mark with its own id key_<i> — so one play command with reveal: [note_0, ...] and press: [key_0, ...] writes the staff note permanently AND presses its piano key transiently on the same beat.
Parameter schema:
{
 "type": "object",
 "properties": {
  "notes": {
   "type": "string",
   "description": "Notation, e.g. \"C4:q D4:q E4:q F4:q G4:h R:q G4+B4:h\". Up to 16 tokens; comfortable range C3-A5. Default: the C-major scale."
  },
  "abc": {
   "type": "string",
   "description": "A tune in ABC notation (overrides `notes`; the first voice is rendered, bar lines follow the tune's M: unless time_top is set)."
  },
  "time_top": {
   "type": "integer",
   "description": "Beats per bar for the bar lines, 2-6 (default 4; 0 = no bar lines)."
  },
  "keyboard": {
   "type": "boolean",
   "description": "Draw a compact piano under the staff; each sounding note also gets its own key-mark element key_<i> — reveal the notes, press the keys (default false; suits the C4-C6 range)."
  },
  "labels": {
   "type": "boolean",
   "description": "Letter names under the notes (default true; false on a grand staff unless set)."
  },
  "clef": {
   "type": "string",
   "enum": [
    "treble",
    "bass",
    "grand"
   ],
   "description": "treble (default); bass for low notes (comfortable C2-E4); grand = treble over bass joined by a brace, for piano music."
  },
  "bass_notes": {
   "type": "string",
   "description": "Grand staff only: the bass staff's notes, the same notation as `notes`, lined up with them by beat. Up to 16 tokens."
  },
  "sound": {
   "type": "boolean",
   "description": "The notes sound as they are drawn: a draw of note_<i> ids plays exactly those notes, each appearing (and its key going down) as it sounds, with the beat's sentence over them. Write no play for them yourself."
  },
  "title": {
   "type": "string"
  }
 }
}
Element ids your commands can reference:
- staff: the five staff lines (a group)
- clef: the clef (treble, or bass on a bass staff; the treble one on a grand staff)
- bass_staff: the lower staff's five lines (grand staff)
- bass_clef: the bass clef (grand staff)
- brace: the brace joining the two staves (grand staff)
- bass_note_<i>: the i-th bass-staff token (grand staff)
- bass_key_<i>: the key mark for bass token i (grand staff with keyboard)
- keys: the compact piano below the staff (a group, when keyboard)
- key_<i>: the key mark for token i (a group, when keyboard) — press these in time with the notes
- note_<i>: the i-th token — heads, stem, flag, ledger lines (a group; rests too)
- bar_<i>: the i-th bar line
- label_<i>: letter name under token i (when labels)
- title: figure title, when set
Examples:
Request: "Write the C major scale on a staff." → params: {"title":"The C major scale"}
Request: "Show a simple melody with a chord at the end." → params: {"notes":"E4:q E4:q F4:q G4:q G4:q F4:q E4:q D4:q C4:h C4+E4+G4:h","title":"Ode to Joy (opening)"}
Request: "How do the two hands share a piano score?" → params: {"clef":"grand","notes":"E4:q E4:q F4:q G4:q G4:q F4:q E4:q D4:q","bass_notes":"C3:h G2:h C3:h G2:h","title":"Two hands, one score"}

In YAML: `template: note_sheet` and `params:` per the schema above; commands name the element ids above.
